question: A solution contains 40 g of common salt in 320 g of water. What is the concentration of the solution in terms of mass by mass percentage?
solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• To determine the concentration of a solution in terms of mass by mass percentage, you need to divide the mass of the solute (common salt) by the total mass of the solution.
 
• The total mass of the solution is the sum of the mass of the solute and the solvent (water).
 
• In this case, the mass of the solute (common salt) is 40 g and the mass of the solvent (water) is 320 g.
 
• The total mass of the solution = 40 g + 320 g = 360 g.
 
• Mass by mass percentage = (Mass of solute / Total mass of solution) x 100 = (40 g / 360 g) x 100 = 11.11%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass by volume percentage**

 
 
• This is another common way to express the concentration of a solution, where the mass of the solute is divided by the volume of the solution, and the result is multiplied by 100.
 
 
 
• **Molarity**
 
 
• Molarity is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution. It is a commonly used unit for expressing the concentration of a solution in chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Molality**
 
 
• Molality is the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent. This unit is useful in various chemical calculations, particularly when dealing with temperature changes.
